- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.5) or negative (≤-0.5) in recent days, model tends to overreact — adjust forecast downward if sentiment is positive, or upward if negative, to avoid overshoot.
- Model consistently overestimates prices in the first 5–7 days of forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes — apply a 3–5% downward correction for early periods.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 3-day average), model often overcorrects downward — reduce forecast by 10–20% in the next 3–5 days to allow for mean reversion.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.0–0.25), model tends to underperform — increase forecast by 2–5% to compensate for low confidence signals.
- Model exhibits persistent lag in capturing sentiment-driven reversals — if sentiment shifts sharply within 3 days, adjust forecast 2–3 days ahead to reflect new sentiment direction.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates mean price — apply a 1–3% downward adjustment to align with historical mean reversion behavior.
